title: Kez Rampage — 4 Gods / Harpy

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY New Patch ★★★ KEZ Rampage Build In Auto Chess

body:
# Kez Rampage — 4 Gods / Harpy

A three-star Kez turned into a rampaging one-man army. The frame is built to keep
him casting and keep the enemy disabled: **4 Gods** slash skill cooldowns so Kez
and Earthshaker chain their abilities, **2 Harpies** add an extra target to
single-target spells, and the **Tauren totems** from Earthshaker plus Elder Titan
disarm, silence, and stun the enemy board almost without pause. A three-star
stealth-assassin Riki slips into the backline to clean up. It comes fully online
at level 9, but the two-star version with the totem lock is already strong from
the mid game.

## Core Units

The two non-negotiables are three-star Kez and three-star Riki; the rest raise
the God count and totem uptime.

| Unit | Cost | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kez | 3 | The three-star carry (Harpy) |
| Riki | 3 | Three-star stealth assassin, backline cleaner |
| Earthshaker | 3 | Totem stuns |
| Elder Titan | 4 | Second Tauren totem (disarm/silence) |
| Rubick | 3 | First Wizard / God |
| Lion | 4 | Second Wizard for multicast |
| Skywrath Mage | 1 | Second Harpy |
| Zeus | 5 | God, late-game flex |
| Mars | 1 | God count, front body |
| Tiny | 2 | Cheap front-line filler |

Elder Titan plus Earthshaker gives the two Tauren totems; add Rubick and Lion (or
Zeus/Mars) to reach **4 Gods** for the cooldown reduction. Skywrath Mage is the
second Harpy alongside Kez, turning his single-target hit into a multi-stun.

## Items

Kez is the only unit you seriously itemise — funnel everything into him.

- **Linkens Sphere** — mandatory in the ultra-late game. Without it, one hex or
  silence permanently locks Kez out of the fight and the build folds; the guide
  lost a game exactly this way.
- **Manta Style** — illusions each proc his damage and tank; the standout carry
  item on a three-star.
- **Battle Fury** (or Radiance) — strong general damage; interchangeable with
  Manta depending on what you find.
- **Satanic** on Riki so he survives a stray hex and keeps cleaning house.
- Late anti-mage tech: **BKB** or magic resist on Kez when the lobby is mage-heavy.

## Relics

- **Stolen Vault** is the safe economy pick for the lose-streak open, especially
  when a second player is contesting Kez — the early gold lead can pressure them
  off the build entirely.
- Avoid Magic Seed here; you want to roll after round 15, not hoard seeds.
- On round 25, take **Frenzy** if you're low or planning to scale, **Guardian**
  if you're healthy and content to coast to top 4.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

The default line is a lose streak anchored by the priest (Dazzle + Shadow Demon)
for healing. Round 3 matters more than it looks: aim to hit 10 gold by then (four
gold to start, plus kill gold), delaying unit sales to bank interest. Prioritise
gold over units in the early rounds, then rush to **level 7**, where tier-3 odds
peak at 35% — that's where Kez, Riki, and Earthshaker live. Take the
roll-cost-reduction talent on round 15 and dismiss the tier-3 units you're missing
(the guide dismissed Humans to also fish Elder Titan and Lion). If a rival is
contesting Kez, level up and complete synergies instead of roll-warring them —
let them stall out or die, then roll into the freed-up pool. The board is
complete at level 9; four Nagas (swap the Wizards to Naga Siren) is the level-10+
answer to heavy mages.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

The totem/stun engine wants the enemy stuck in place, so cluster your disablers
where Earthshaker and Elder Titan cover the most bodies. Position Kez to summon
his Manta illusions into the front so they immediately soak and deal damage.
Elder Titan being three-star matters defensively — he tends to eat enemy Cipher
Vice / hexes that would otherwise land on Kez. The comp is strong into most
physical and god boards but is vulnerable to **mages** (splash Naga Siren for
magic resist) and to **physical burst like Techies** targeting Kez directly. The
hard counter is anything that permanently controls Kez — hex, stun-lock, or Doom
— which is exactly why Linkens Sphere is non-negotiable.
